title: Uttarakhand Minister Rekha Arya's Husband Arrested in Jhansi After October FIR
excerpt: Dehradun police said Girdhari Lal Sahu was held outside a university campus in Jhansi in the case registered on October 15 on his wife's complaint, and a second accused was arrested in Udham Singh Nagar.
body:
• Uttarakhand Police arrested Girdhari Lal Sahu, husband of Cabinet Minister Rekha Arya, in Uttar Pradesh's Jhansi district, Dehradun SSP Pramendra Dobhal told ANI on Saturday.
  • A case was registered on October 15 following Arya's complaint, with charges including forgery and serious offences under the SC/ST Act, the SSP said.
  • A second accused, Satyendra Thakur, was arrested near Kichha in Udham Singh Nagar district, and both men were being sent to judicial custody, police said.
  • Police said Sahu has over 44 cases registered against him, with convictions in some and others still pending.

Uttarakhand Police have arrested Girdhari Lal Sahu, also known as Pappu Girdhari, the husband of state Cabinet Minister Rekha Arya, in Uttar Pradesh's Jhansi district, officials said on Saturday. Speaking to ANI, Dehradun SSP Pramendra Dobhal said Sahu was arrested on charges of forgery as well as serious offences under the SC/ST Act.

Sahu was arrested on Friday evening outside a private university campus in Jhansi district after he had been absconding for some time, according to ANI's account of the police briefing. A second accused, Satyendra Thakur, was arrested near Kichha in Udham Singh Nagar district. Both accused were being sent to judicial custody, the SSP said.

The Police Account

"A case was registered against Girdhari Lal Sahu on October 15, following a complaint filed by the Cabinet Minister, Rekha Arya. The charges include forgery as well as serious offences under the SC/ST Act," Dobhal told ANI. He said a nine-member special team was constituted for the investigation and arrested the two men, and that any other individuals whose names emerge would also face legal action.

"Girdhari Lal Sahu has an extensive criminal history; over 44 cases have been registered against him. He has previously been convicted in some of these cases, while others remain pending."

— Pramendra Dobhal, Dehradun SSP, speaking to ANI

The SSP also said police had confirmed that forgery was used to remove Rekha Arya from her position as a director of a company and to install Satyendra Thakur as a director in her place. Police said they would present the accused before the court and seek judicial remand, and that further steps would be taken to gather evidence.

What the Original Complaint Alleged

Arya, Uttarakhand's women empowerment and child development minister, lodged the FIR against her husband at the Cantt police station in Dehradun under various sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, ANI reported. Prashant News, reporting the filing in October, said the FIR invoked provisions relating to criminal conspiracy, cheating, forgery, bigamy, cruelty by a husband, voluntarily causing hurt, intentional insult and criminal intimidation, alongside provisions of the SC/ST Act.

In her complaint, Arya alleged that when she opposed her husband's alleged relationships with other women, he began physically assaulting her, abusing her and threatening to kill her. She alleged that on several occasions he used caste-based derogatory remarks to insult her in the presence of staff at her official residence. She further alleged that forged signatures and fake documents were used to show her as having been removed as a director in companies, and that she had neither signed such documents nor submitted any resignation.

Prashant News reported that Arya also shared two audio clips on social media and claimed in her complaint that a recording captured Sahu speaking to a woman about conspiring to kill her. That report noted the allegations had not been independently verified, and that Sahu was not available for comment at the time of the filing. After posting a video on social media, Arya's health deteriorated and she was taken to hospital and kept under observation, police said in that earlier report.

What Happens Next

With both men in custody, the case now moves to court proceedings and the continuing police investigation the SSP described. Police said evidence gathering would continue and that further legal action would follow if other names emerge in the investigation. The allegations in the FIR remain allegations to be tested in court; the arrest itself, and the criminal-history account given at the briefing, are the facts police stated publicly on Saturday.
nri_angle: The arrest of a sitting Uttarakhand cabinet minister's husband, on her own complaint, is a closely watched accountability case in Indian state politics.
author: Diaspora Desk
